content: The server racks hummed like a chorus of dying insects, their blinking LEDs casting a sickly blue glow over the cold concrete floor. I leaned against a towering blade chassis, the heat radiating off it like the last breath of a fever dream, while my fingers traced the edge of a corrupted drive—its secrets buried deeper than a mobster’s ledger. Across the aisle, the night-shift admin slumped in his chair, his bloodshot eyes locked on the flickering monitor, sweat beading on his forehead like he’d just seen something he wasn’t supposed to. The air smelled of ozone and burnt silicon, the kind of stink that clings to lies. Somewhere in the labyrinth of cables and code, the truth was waiting, but it wasn’t gonna come easy—nothing ever does in this town.
